instr:
Identify the target series, measured quantity, entity, recording frequency, and history and forecast bounds from its description. Read all documents, but give direct target statements, explicit hypothetical scenarios (“suppose,” “assume”), and supplied reference values priority over conflicting logs, reports, investigations, plans, and predictions. Apply another entity’s event only when a statement explicitly connects it to the target; an explicit exclusion means it does not apply. Titles, official formatting, technical detail, and repeated claims do not establish relevance.

Build a timeline of supported intervals. Use “measurement_error” for unreliable, noisy, unreasonable, corrupted, or miscalibrated readings, including separate entries for separate stated windows. End each error at its stated resolution. A repair or update alone does not establish a lasting real baseline change; require independent, explicit evidence of one. Use “one_off_disturbance” for a temporary real past effect when nonrecurrence is stated. Preserve the precise scope of nonrecurrence: “not again this week,” “not expected this year,” and “not in the future” have different horizons. Use “state” for each supported on-interval of a real continuing condition. An event can support both a temporary disturbance and a state when both effects are explicitly stated. Use “future_event” for an explicitly expected forecast change, including an increase after a scheduled event, a continuing trend, or an anticipated stop. Distinguish observed, hypothetical, and expected effects; do not replace direct evidence with a speculative explanation.

Use “recurring_pattern” when repetition is stated or timestamped values demonstrate multiple cycles. For a supplied reference profile, use only sampled timestamps that directly support each daily window; include the complete relevant profile as evidence. Do not interpolate exact boundaries between samples, extend beyond supported dates, or treat one several-hour window as recurring.

For every entry provide ISO start/end timestamps, recurrence (none/daily/weekly/every_n_days), daily_start/daily_end (HH:MM) and every_n_days when applicable, recurs_in_future (true/false), direction (up/down/none), and complete verbatim supporting quote text. Include the series description when it establishes target, frequency, or bounds, and all adjacent clauses needed to connect cause, effect, timing, resolution, and nonrecurrence. Never truncate quotes or invent timing or magnitude. Convert stated durations to endpoints using the series frequency. Return an empty list if no applicable effect is supported.

Natural cycles are NOT anomalies: regular daily/weekly/seasonal behaviour of the measured quantity (e.g. zero solar irradiance at night, lower weekend traffic, overnight lows) must never be reported as measurement_error, one_off_disturbance or recurring_pattern to repair.
